question: A number of countries are expanding their water infrastructure in response to droughts. For example, Morocco has earmarked almost EUR 13 billion for its 2020-2027 programme (dams, desalination and reuse). India is investing around EUR 4.2 billion in its Ken-Betwa project. China spent nearly EUR 757 billion on water infrastructure projects between 2021 and 2025. The EU’s water resilience strategy focuses more on saving water than on developing new resources. 1.

Does the Commission have a detailed, comprehensive overview of investments made and planned in each Member State, and financed from EU, national or private funds, broken down by investment type (water savings, treatment, storage, wastewater reuse or desalination)?
How much additional storage and how much extra water annually will these investments bring, particularly to the farming industry?

Has the Commission assessed whether these investments will actually provide enough water to meet farmers’ needs? If they will not, what targets and funding will it put in place to increase the available resources?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Jean-Paul Garraud (PfE).
